summary: Codex Sinaiticus Syrus / Codex Sinaiticus Syriacus / Syriac Sinaiticus

layer.label: Syriac Undertext: Dormition of the Virgin Mary

location.repository: St. Catherine's Monastery of the Sinai

note.value: Pencil foliation beginning with '4', intending to include exposed unnumbered front pastedown as f. 1
Quires are established according to natural movement of folios and do not correspond to original Georgian quire signatures in overtext
Unbound quires until f. 150; large number of singletons at the beginning and end of quires (usually quinions) that may originally have been bifolios belonging to a quire
Quire signatures are marked in the bottom inner margin of the last folio of each quire; quires of 10 ff. A later hand provided the quire signatures in Georgian that run backwards
Reinforced leather. Large parts missing in front; back cover in two vertical parts, reattached with thread; exposed spine.
The presence of quire signatures in Georgian, probably by a binder, points to the fact the manuscript was probably in Palestine between the 9th and the 10th c. CE
Most folios severely cockled, with raised ridges appearing as glossy; various degrees of discoloration, at least in part due to application of liquid in the course of prior scholarly investigation
This is the well-known Codex Sinaiticus Syriacus

program.description: Catalogued as part of UCLA Library's "Identification and Description of the Syriac and Arabic Manuscripts at St. Catherine’s Monastery of the Sinai, Phase 1: Syriac Parchment Manuscripts" project (2022-2025), funded by the National Endowment for the Humanities. Principle cataloguers were Grigory Kessel (Lead cataloguer), Natalia Smelova (Associate cataloguer), and Vevian Zaki (Cataloguer for Arabic content in Syriac manuscripts).

program.label: Sinai Palimpsests Project
program.description: Imaged and studied as part of the Sinai Palimpsests Project (2011–2016), a collaboration between St. Catherine’s Monastery of the Sinai, the Early Manuscripts Electronic Library, and UCLA Library, funded by the Arcadia Fund and the Ahmanson Foundation. The project used multispectral imaging and scholarly analysis to recover and document erased and obscured texts in palimpsest manuscripts from the monastery’s collection.
